A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Time-MQA framework and TSQA dataset. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations in Tables 3–4, forecasting and reasoning examples, and a 78-participant user study with results in Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds numerical-input ablation experiments in Appendix E and Table 6. The user study appears in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The context-conditioned QA framework, LoRA-based continual pretraining, and Mistral 7B, Llama-3 8B, and Qwen-2.5 7B backbones remain unchanged. The new input perturbations are evaluation controls, not changes to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds testing with missing, Gaussian-replaced, and shuffled numeric inputs within existing QA tasks. Section 3.2.1 also stops listing NASA Series among anomaly-detection sources, although unchanged dataset totals do not establish whether underlying records changed. Table 5 primarily documents existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains the same three tuned models and GPT-4o and Doubao comparators. Table 4 retains zero-shot Mistral, and the user study retains its four models. Appendix E introduces input conditions without adding a competing method.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces four-condition testing on 50 MCQs and 50 true/false questions, with manually reassigned labels for random and shuffled inputs. Sections 4.1–4.2 remove references to considering source ratios during training-sample selection and domains during evaluation-sample selection. These revise the reported protocol without establishing reruns; training budgets and main metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V1 includes a tuned-versus-zero-shot comparison and illustrative cases but no controlled numerical-input reliance study. V2 adds systematic removal, Gaussian replacement, and shuffling experiments for Mistral and Qwen in Appendix E. These directly investigate whether answers depend on numeric inputs and temporal structure, substantially extending the diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for model performance. The new ablation reports point accuracies and N/A outcomes without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 and the user-study results remain unchanged. Table 6 adds perturbation results: for example, Qwen achieves 0.98 true/false and 0.74 MCQ accuracy with random inputs, while missing-input outcomes are N/A. These are newly evaluated conditions with manually relabelled targets, rather than same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same time-series and context definitions and mapping f: (X, C, Q) → A. No new formal assumptions, propositions, derivations, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: unified contextual time-series QA, approximately 200k TSQA pairs across twelve domains and five tasks, and improved capabilities through continual pretraining. The new experiments support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly limits financial coverage to earnings-call transcripts. Appendix E adds an interpretation of models' sensitivity to numeric inputs and acknowledges that higher random-series accuracy can arise from easier, generic answers rather than deeper understanding. Existing performance interpretations and other limitations remain.

D1.justification: New Table 5 provides task-by-domain counts, source mappings, and real/synthetic labels; Appendix B clarifies measured signals versus generated QA. V2 changes the resource namespace from Time-QA to Time-MQA and removes the financial-data exception from its public-availability statement. The abstract drops its explicit executable-code disclosure. Training hyperparameters and serialization templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds source references for NAB, SensorScope, UCR, KPI, MIT-BIH, MGAB, and Yahoo, supporting the new provenance table. The related-work discussion and positioning against existing time-series and QA approaches remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes local grammar, terminology, cross-reference, and author-information edits and adds acknowledgments. Two new appendix sections shift Training Data Format from C to D and User Study from D to F. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 5–6, adjusts table presentation, and reflows the appendices. Figure 4's expanded caption explains that its task and domain rings have no segment-wise correspondence, and Table 3's caption clarifies metric directions. Existing illustrations, forecasting plots, and user-study charts retain their content.

improvement.justification: V2 improves dataset transparency through Table 5 and adds direct numerical-input controls in Table 6, addressing an evidential gap in v1. It also clarifies financial coverage and cautions against interpreting random-input accuracy as deeper understanding. These gains are bounded by the small, manually relabelled ablation, unscored missing-input outcomes, and absent uncertainty estimates; the main benchmark evidence remains unchanged.
